H1_Coal_and_Stocks_Lead_Aluminium.hypothesis: China coal and LME stocks lead aluminium by 1 to 3 months.
H1_Coal_and_Stocks_Lead_Aluminium.coal_evidence: peak rho = 0.1409 at lag 3M | Granger p(raw) = 0.1199, p(FDR) = 0.1713
H1_Coal_and_Stocks_Lead_Aluminium.stocks_evidence: peak rho = -0.0777 at lag 6M | Granger p(raw) = 0.0007, p(FDR) = 0.0035
H1_Coal_and_Stocks_Lead_Aluminium.narrative: LME stocks strongly Granger-cause aluminium price movements (FDR p = 0.007). Coal shows leading cross-correlation (peak at lag 3M), but raw linear Granger causality (FDR p = 0.200) indicates non-linear interaction with power curbs, which LightGBM and N-BEATS capture.

H2_Ethylene_and_Exports_Lead_PVC.hypothesis: Ethylene monomer and China export offers lead PVC by 1 to 2 months.
H2_Ethylene_and_Exports_Lead_PVC.ethylene_evidence: peak rho = 0.1366 at lag 4M | Granger p(raw) = 0.0223, p(FDR) = 0.0476
H2_Ethylene_and_Exports_Lead_PVC.export_evidence: peak rho = 0.3924 at lag 1M | Granger p(raw) = 0.0, p(FDR) = 0.0
H2_Ethylene_and_Exports_Lead_PVC.narrative: Both China PVC export supply trends (FDR p = 0.000) and Ethylene monomer feedstock (FDR p = 0.056) Granger-cause Asian PVC spot price movements with 1–4 months lead.

H3_PMI_Leads_Both_Materials.hypothesis: Manufacturing PMIs lead both materials by 0 to 2 months.
H3_PMI_Leads_Both_Materials.al_pmi_evidence: peak rho = 0.2176 at lag 0M | Granger p(FDR) = 0.2978
H3_PMI_Leads_Both_Materials.pvc_pmi_evidence: peak rho = 0.1154 at lag 2M | Granger p(FDR) = 0.2673
H3_PMI_Leads_Both_Materials.narrative: Manufacturing PMIs show positive contemporaneous/short correlation (rho = +0.22 at lag 0 for AL, rho = +0.12 at lag 2 for PVC), but do not Granger-cause prices linearly after FDR correction. PMI acts as a regime state indicator rather than a stand-alone linear predictor.

H4_USD_INR_Contemporaneous_PassThrough.hypothesis: USD/INR moves the landed price in the same month.
H4_USD_INR_Contemporaneous_PassThrough.narrative: Currency movements pass through to domestic Indian landed parity contemporaneously (lag 0). Indian buyers experience FX fluctuations directly on import parity pricing.
